title: Low-protein medical foods & specialty foods
source_note: Compiled July 2026 from manufacturer sites, low-protein food retailers (PKU Perspectives, Nutricia Store, Save Rite Medical), PKU family shopping guides (Vitafriends, NSPKU), distributor announcements, and peer-reviewed cost studies. Covers low-protein modified foods and specialty medical foods marketed to the PKU/IEM community; amino-acid protein-substitute formulas are a separate dataset and are excluded (a few GMP-based 'milk' drinks that straddle food/formula are flagged in notes). Prices are indicative retail points in the currency shown and vary by retailer, pack size, and prescription status.

records.product_line: Low-protein modified food annual cost per patient
records.price_note: US low-protein foods ~$1,274-1,961/yr per patient (formula separate); total PKU treatment est. $19,057-$54,147/yr; UK pharmacy markups 200-300% over manufacturing cost
records.notes: 98% of special low-protein food subgroups cost more than regular/'free-from' equivalents; ~60% of US families pay out of pocket, driving price sensitivity and adherence gaps.

sources.title: Special Low Protein Foods Prescribed in England: Prescribing & Cost (PMC8620831)
PKU Patients, Families Burdened by High Treatment Costs

records.price_note: Some US states cap low-protein-food coverage at ~$3,000/yr; UK/EU largely prescription-reimbursed
records.notes: EU markets run on physician prescription + reimbursement (favoring Nutricia/Mevalia/Promin); US is a patchwork of state mandates, caps and out-of-pocket, favoring direct/retail sellers (Cambrooke, PKU Perspectives).
